findings.title: K000156741: BIG-IP APM vulnerability CVE-2025-53521
findings.summary_md: F5's advisory, page shows Published Date Oct 15, 2025 and Updated Date Apr 1, 2026. Originally categorized and remediated as a DoS flaw at CVSS 7.5 (v3.1) / 8.7 (v4.0), it was re-categorized in March 2026 to an unauthenticated RCE in the apmd process, CWE-121 stack-based buffer overflow, internal ID 1977933, at CVSS 9.8 (v3.1) / 9.3 (v4.0), exploited in the wild and also affecting Appliance mode. It lists fixes 17.5.1.3 and 17.1.3 (17.x), 16.1.6.1 (16.x), and 15.1.10.8 (15.x), points to IoC article K000160486 for activity c05d5254 and compromise guidance K11438344, and warns that UCS backups taken after a compromise can contain persistent malware.

findings.title: CISA Adds One Known Exploited Vulnerability to Catalog
findings.summary_md: CISA alert with release date March 27, 2026 adding CVE-2025-53521, F5 BIG-IP Remote Code Execution Vulnerability, to the KEV Catalog based on evidence of active exploitation. Under BOD 22-01 it set a remediation deadline for FCEB agencies of midnight Monday March 30, 2026, the earliest government acknowledgment that the flaw was being exploited.

findings.title: Hackers exploiting critical F5 BIG-IP flaw in attacks, patch now
findings.summary_md: First coverage of the reclassification, by Sergiu Gatlan, March 30, 2026 06:59 AM ET. It reports F5's advisory update published the previous Sunday confirming attackers exploit CVE-2025-53521 to deploy webshells on unpatched devices, with IoCs in article K000160486 and checks of disks, logs, and terminal history recommended. Shadowserver at the time tracked over 240,000 BIG-IP instances exposed online, and CISA had KEV-listed the bug on Friday March 27 with a March 30 federal deadline.

findings.title: ESET Research on PoisonedRefresh: two related malware components on BIG-IP systems
findings.summary_md: Original researcher disclosure of the PoisonedRefresh name, post timestamped 2026-04-24T16:10:45Z. ESET says it discovered two related malware components on VirusTotal, that a umount component infects /usr/sbin/httpd by prepending a malicious ELF binary, and publishes SHA-1 IoCs E5066C2490197FFBE0E916BC232114A61CB09A16 and 7A2FC3510B502D8FDC2548F907AF08308840851C, pointing defenders to F5's K000160486 because benign functionality is preserved and F5's advisory should be followed to identify compromise.

findings.title: Dissecting a PHP web server rootkit
findings.summary_md: Sophos X-Ops technical analysis by Luke Mitchell dated September 7, 2026 on the Sophos Threat Research listing (first Wayback capture 2026-09-07T19:54:18Z), one day before the story's first event. It details the second-stage implant: RC4-hidden strings with key TrswBWIl90Z5e38n, interception of __libc_start_main, hooking of apr_dso_load and apr_time_now, mmap-level injection of a web shell using magic prefix BSOHAzPB into apm_css.php3, full_wt.php3, and webtop_popup_css.php3, HTTP 201 with text/css replies, an authenticated AF_UNIX backdoor at /run/bigtlog.pipe with token Kzwd6jM5 handing stdio to /bin/bash, an umount installer with a 0x5430-byte prefix persisting across upgrade images, detection as Linux/Agnt-IC, and sample SHA256 26bd5b0722d1dbab5db749a063c49bc8638653ac2addfead7a9cb3d6d57bccc9.
